title: Deactivate and Reactivate Kueue Workload
description: Last resort: re-admit a stuck GKE Kueue workload (e.g. after preemption) by toggling its spec.active property to false and back to true. Historical mitigation for a known Kueue readmission issue (marked FIXED 2026-04-14). active=false evicts the workload, so run it only when the workload has 0 pods left.
instruction:
Last resort, run by the queue/cluster owner. `spec.active=false` evicts the workload and `spec.active=true` lets Kueue re-admit it at once.
Preconditions (all must hold):
1. The workload is stuck in `QuotaReserved` / `Requeued` while capacity is available, and your Kueue version predates the fix (see [[gotchas-kubernetes-gke]], gotcha 6).
2. It has 0 pods left: `kubectl get pods -n <ns> | grep <jobset-name>` returns nothing (no Terminating pods) and `kubectl get events -n <ns> --field-selector reason=FailedKillPod` is empty. If pods are stuck Terminating, do not kick: a re-admitted TPU slice can be formed on TPUs the old containers still hold. Follow [[kueue-stuck-termination-recovery]] instead.
Then: `kubectl patch workload ${workload_name} -n <ns> --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"active":false}}'`, wait about 5 s, and `kubectl patch workload ${workload_name} -n <ns> --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"active":true}}'`.

workload_name.description: Name of the GKE Kueue workload to re-admit
